text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Homeland Union leader Vytautas Landsbergis called "hasty and unacceptable" the suggestion by President Algirdas Brazauskas unilaterally to set the sea border with Latvia. Lithuania's parliament will today consider two draft documents on the disputed territory in the Baltic Sea.

- The president of the Confederation of Industrialists of Lithuania Bronislovas Lubys suggested to Brazauskas that he appoint the Homeland Union's Gediminas Vagnorius to be the new prime minister after the party won the first round of elections.

- The parliamentary faction of the Homeland Union intends to oppose the energy ministry recommendation on raising electricity and heating prices by a third. The new government will not talk about energy price rises untill the real income of the population increases, Vagnorius told Energy Minister Saulius Kutas and Finance Minister Algimantas Krizhinauskas.
- 28 employees of the bankrupt Mazheikiai Furniture company resumed their hunger strike in front of parliament on Monday, demanding unpaid salaries.
- Energy Minister Saulius Kutas informed the Homeland Union parliament faction that Lithuania has 300,000 tonnes of heating oil and needs another 340,000 tonnes for the winter.
- The energy ministry drew up a draft project to increase heating and electricity prices by a third starting January 1, 1997.

- The Board of the Bank of Lithuania refused to issue a permit to Polish Kredyt Bank to open its first office in Vilnius as not all the necessary documents were submitted. The bank is the first foreign bank to want to open in Lithuania.

- According to the newspaper, based on nine month reports, Snoras Bank is ranked second among commercial banks and shows its intention to become a retail bank and compete with the favourite among small depositors, Lithuanian Savings Bank.

- Analysts say Hermis Bank is lagging only a little behind market leader Vilnius Bank and in some areas in the first half of the year showed better results. Some dealers predict that Hermis Bank shares are worth 70 litas and may rise to 130 litas next year.
